Sopa de capirotada. — Take cold French bread, slice it very thin and place it in the tortera with a little refrito of tomato, garlic and onion with its fine spices that you will have prepared in regular quantity to place on top of the refrito a layer of bread, and on top of that another layer of refrito, a powder of Flemish cheese grated and a little egg that you will have ready as if to lamprear, and so you cover the tortera until finished, leaving on top a little egg. The slices of bread are broken with a little broth from the cooking so that they do not remain dry nor loose. Place the tortera on a stove with little fire and on top a comal with little fire as well.

pan á lo largo, y delgadas, y se tuestan en la parrilla de red
sin que se quemen, después se fríen otros pedacitos de pan
delgados, con tocino magro, asadura de cabrito ó de aves, y
cuando está hecha la fritura se echa un poco de perejil y
huevos duros bien picado, un poco de queso rallado, clavo
y canela en corta cantidad y retírese del fuego. Pónganse
en la cazuela ó* sopera una capa del pan tostado que hemos
dicho primero, y otra capa del picado hecho después, y así
hasta concluir: en seguida se hecha caldo del cocido 6 sus-

fa, pájaros fritos, pechugas de ave, rodajitas de huevo, etc.

dad que la carne, se pican jitomates, cebollas y ajos como

38. Bread soup seasoned. — Slices of good bread are cut lengthwise and thinly, and toasted on a wire grill without burning; then other small pieces of bread, thin, are fried with lean bacon, kid offal or fowl offal, and when the frying is done, a little parsley and hard-boiled eggs, well chopped, are added, a little grated cheese, cloves and cinnamon in small quantity, and it is removed from the fire. A layer of the toasted bread mentioned first is placed in the casserole or soup tureen, and another layer of the chopped mixture made afterward, and so on until finished: then broth from the boiled meat or meat substance is poured in to moisten it, and it is placed on the fire, adding a little more broth to bring it to a boil, removing it immediately, and if it becomes very dry, more broth can be added, but in small quantity; once the soup is cooked, an egg mixture is made and poured over it, covering the soup tureen or casserole with a lid, and some embers of fire are placed on top to brown it. If desired for decoration, artichoke hearts, fried birds, fowl breasts, slices of egg, etc., can be placed on top.

39. Meat soup. — A piece of veal meat is put to cook in the pot, and once it is half-cooked (rather tender than firm), it is chopped into small pieces; pieces of the same size are cut from raw potatoes in equal quantity to the meat, tomatoes, onions and garlic are chopped as if making another kind of soup. The broth from the pot is poured in sufficient quantity into a casserole on the fire, adding the chopped garlic, tomatoes and onions, a regular spoonful of butter, the meat and the potatoes. It is brought to a boil, and when this is well cooked, breadcrumbs are added to thicken it, but not in such quantity that it becomes like atole. If the broth remains somewhat loose when placed in the soup tureen, it is buttered. Only pepper is added to the spices, in small quantity.

41. Sopa de tortuga. — Sacada la tortuga de la conoha se
pone á cocer y luego que lo está se pica, dejándolo todo en
el caldo en que se ha cocido, se pone á freir recaudo, oom-
puesto de cebollinos, perejil y un poco de jitomate. Cuando
está frito se echa la carne picada y el caldo, y todo se pone
á cocer á fuego manso. Se muele un poco de canela, clavo y
pimienta y se echa en el caldo. Después se muelen cuatro
yemas de huevo, se hace un caldo compuesto de agua y ha-
rina, y si no queda espeso se freirá mas harina, que se echa-
rá en el caldo con media botella de vino de Oporto, de Ma-
dera ó de Jerez y media de vino de Burdeos. Al ponérsela
sopa en la mesa se la adorna con unas ruedas de huevo.

excerpts.translation: 41. Turtle soup. — Once the turtle has been removed from the shell, it is put to boil, and once it is cooked, it is chopped, leaving everything in the broth in which it has been cooked. A garnish, composed of chives, parsley, and a little tomato, is put to fry. When it is fried, the chopped meat and the broth are added, and everything is put to simmer over low heat. A little cinnamon, clove, and pepper are ground and added to the broth. Then four egg yolks are ground, a broth composed of water and flour is made, and if it does not remain thick, more flour is fried, which is added to the broth with half a bottle of Port, Madeira, or Sherry wine and half a bottle of Bordeaux wine. When the soup is placed on the table, it is garnished with slices of egg.

dientes de ajo machacados y allí se fríe la tortilla hasta que
quede tiesa. Luego se saca la tortilla, se fríe jitomate y ce-
bolla picada, se vuelve á echar allí la tortilla con caldo su-
ficiente, una rama de epazote y unos pedazos de chile ancho
por encima.
44. Otra. — Se coge medio de tortillas chiquitas que se di-
viden en cuartos y se fríen en manteca. Se pica una cebo-
lla y un jitomate, se muele cuartilla de acelgas cocidas, tres
dientes de ajo fritos y tres pimientas gordas. Todo se fríe,
se cuece chorizon, lomo de puerco y jamón, se hace trocitos
y se fríe, y el agua en que se coció todo esto sirve para el
caldillo. Se echa en el el recaudo frito con una cucharada
de aceite, medio de vinagre, un puño de queso rallado y sal
al gusto. Se echa un poco de caldo en la cazuela, una capa
de tortillas, una de queso y otra de chorizon, jamón y lo-
mo y asi sucesivamente hasta que se llena la cazuela y se
pone á dos fuegos.

43. Tortilla soup. — Lard is burned with three crushed garlic cloves and the tortilla is fried there until it becomes stiff. Then the tortilla is removed, tomato and chopped onion are fried, the tortilla is put back there with sufficient broth, a sprig of epazote and some pieces of ancho chili on top.

44. Another. — Half of small tortillas are taken which are divided into quarters and fried in lard. One onion and one tomato are chopped, quarter of cooked chard is ground, three cloves of fried garlic and three allspices. Everything is fried, chorizo, pork loin and ham are boiled, cut into small pieces and fried, and the water in which all this was boiled serves for the broth. The fried seasoning is added with one spoonful of oil, half of vinegar, a handful of grated cheese and salt to taste. Some broth is poured into the casserole, a layer of tortillas, one of cheese and another of chorizo, ham and loin and so on successively until the casserole is filled and placed over two fires.

Bread soup with oysters. — A sofrito is made of onion, tomato, and garlic, adding a whole chili with fine spices of clove, cinnamon, and pepper with a piece of ancho chili so that it takes color. The oysters, already washed with their own water, are added to the dry sofrito, because they themselves release a lot of water after being cooked. Rice soup, Cuban ajiaco. — The rice, very well washed, is put to boil with the broth that is deemed necessary; garlic, along with a little onion and a tomato, are separately fried in oil, and, after adding a few drops of lemon juice, they are mixed in when removing it from the heat; care is taken to stir it very well, and after resting for a while, it can be eaten.

pan partido en pedacitos redondos ó cuadrados, y después

excerpts.translation: 64. Gazpacho (soup bowl). — A soup bowl is rubbed with raw garlic, and then oil, cumin, pepper, and salt are added, and beaten until well mixed; then bread cut into small round or square pieces is placed in it, and after having been stirred in the soup bowl, cold water is poured in, leaving it thus for a while until the bread swells, and at the moment of serving vinegar is added so that the bread does not sour, and some slices of cucumber, tomato, pepper, and onion may be added.

cho, uno de tuétano, dos cebollas enteras y una cabeza de

jas de canela, todo; molido y sé agrega al caldillo jamón pi-
cado, yerbas, tomillo y orégano, zanahorias y nabo. Des-
pués se pone la olla á fuego manso, se le echa riño Jeras
ó Malaga y un poco de vinagre, ya que está sazonado se va-
cía en una cacerola poniéndose en rescoldo á que dé un her-
yor con la sopa, y si le falto vino se le echa para servir
la sopa.

carne de ternera ó* de carnero una 6 dos libras de garban-

servirse; si se quiere que tenga mayor sustancia, se muele

baza, una berengena, un poco de malanga, un pedazo de

do una pasta, se deslíe con caldo de la olla, y se echan en

olla, y un poco de polvo de pimienta.

excerpts.translation:
92. Spanish stew — Put into it 1 or 2 pounds of veal or mutton, 1 or 2 pounds of chickpeas, in proportion and soaked from the previous night. Add to it a good slice of raw lean ham, and poultry offal. When it boils, skim it and add the salt. After a boil of half an hour, remove the necessary broth for the sauce you wish to prepare. Add to the stew the legumes, which will be boiled separately. Before everything is well cooked, add a chorizo. When served, put the meats in one casserole, and the legumes in another with a jitomate sauce or parsley sauce. To make the first, cut three jitomates and pass them through a sieve; once done, put them in a casserole with the broth that was set aside, adding cumin, salt, and vinegar. Let everything boil for a moment and pour into the sauce boat. To make the second, grind very green parsley mixed with bread crumbs, and put both things in a casserole with broth, salt, and vinegar, letting it boil for a good while and stirring with a wooden spoon so that it thins, and serve.

93. Putrid stew. — Put the chickpeas and meat as has been said, skim it, and then add a hen, bacon, ham, pig’s feet and ear, stuffed and poultry offal.

94. Vegetable stew. — This stew differs from the others only in that the vegetables are cooked with the meat, bacon, etc.; care must be taken to add them after the meat has cooked well; it is seasoned with some spices; this is the custom in Andalusia.

95. Sick person’s stew or pot. — It is usually made with hen or mutton, adding, if it is to be substantial, some chickpeas and ham; the broth must be cooked before serving; if you want it to have more substance, grind the hen on the metate with bread crumbs and thin it in broth, then strain it, and seasoned, put it on the fire, but without boiling.

96. Restaurant stew. — Add to the common pot an old hen, a piece of lean beef and another of veal, two 41 carrots, onions, leeks, a bunch of fragrant herbs, a clear of spice, and cook until reduced to one third; and then remove the fat.

97. French-style stew. — Cook one pound of meat in three quarts of water, with salt, letting it cook slowly and skimming it well; then add some carrot, turnip, parsley, clove of spice, garlic, and a toasted onion, or well a little burnt sugar to give color to the broth; it must cook five hours over low heat, and with the broth, after straining, make the soup. It is also common to add some poultry offal.

98. Cuban pot. — Prepare a medium casserole with water up to half; add a little salt, two pounds of veal from the kidney area, a piece of ham, a handful of chickpeas already soaked from the previous night, and one pound of fresh pork; add a quarter of a hen and put to cook, taking care to remove the foam. After it has boiled for about an hour, add, well peeled and cleaned, one plantain with its peel, a chorizo, a handful of green beans, half a cabbage, a piece of pumpkin, an eggplant, a little malanga, a piece of Castilla pumpkin, two turnips, two sweet potatoes, four jitomates, two chayotes, an onion, and a piece of pumpkin; let everything boil for another hour, and take care to remove the foam that it throws up again, and to season it, grind a little salt, two or three garlic cloves, some cumin seeds and coriander with two of pepper, and once all is a paste, thin it with broth from the pot, and add it to the same, with two threads of crumbled saffron; let it boil for a while, and serve.

42

99. Mexican putrid pot. — Once the water is boiling, add veal, mutton, pig’s feet, hen, Toluca meat, ham, chorizo, blood sausage, and chickpeas. Once the pot is skimmed, add spine or pork meat, heads of garlic according to the size of the pot, whole onions, spearmint, one ground ancho chili with cumin, spices, coriander, rice, and cover the pot as best as possible so that it boils and has little broth left. Tie a cabbage with a string and put to cook, and some peeled turnips; and when the cabbage is cooked, chop onion and garlic, fry them, and into this add the cabbage, adding peas, green beans, green broad beans, and all kinds of vegetables. Also add to the putrid pot Castilla pumpkin, sweet potato, pears, plantain, etc. To the vegetables while they are frying, add broth from the pot, and a little pepper powder.

226. Catalan stew. — The meat is cut into pieces and put to fry in a pot until the water it releases is reduced. Then a good amount of coarsely chopped onion is added, left to brown, and ground tomatoes are added so that they too brown. Once this is done, the necessary water and a little vinegar, bay leaf, thyme, and oregano are added, the pot is covered with a napkin and an upside-down plate, and it is put over very gentle heat. Clove, cinnamon, and pepper are ground with four or five almonds, with their shells, and added to the meat. When the meat is nearly cooked, enough raw potatoes are fried, a little sherry wine and a spoonful of Catalan brandy are added to the stew, and shortly thereafter the potatoes, and thus it is left almost without fire so that it finishes cooking by the heat of the embers.

227. Stewed pulp. — The meat is roasted with cloves, pepper, garlic, and sliced ham; once roasted, it is fried in lard. Some turnips are peeled, sliced, and fried until they brown, then ground with a little fried bread. Onion and garlic cut into cloves are fried in a pot, wine, vinegar, and the corresponding salt are added, and it is left to cook over gentle heat, taking care that it remains of a regular thickness.

313. Sheep’s blood:— Put water to boil in a saucepan, and when it boils, add the cooked and sliced blood. Put oil and butter in a frying pan, and fry the slices of blood well. Separately, chop a good amount of tomato and onion with a little garlic and fry; once well fried, add the blood that was set aside, add a small amount of water, cloves, pepper, ground cinnamon, parsley, oregano, thyme, and cook. It should remain with little broth. Garnish with pickles and olives.

314. Sheep’s blood:— Put a saucepan with water and, once it boils vigorously, add the blood with a little salt and let it cook without breaking apart; then remove and slice into thin slices, put butter and oil in the frying pan and fry the slices, or rather blanch them, since leaving them to fry makes them hard. Chop a good amount of tomato, onion, and a little garlic and put to fry in the same frying pan.

405. Costillas con pulque, — Se atan las costillas á la boca
do una olla, en la cual se echará un cuartillo de pulque por
cada seis costillas, medio pocilio de vino de Jerez y otro
tanto de agua, ajos machacados, tomillo mexicano y pimien-
ta marta jada. Tápese la olla con un trapo. Hágase una sal-
sa con un cuartillo de leche y un puñado de harina, y éche-
sele poco á poco y á medida que se van calentando las cos-
tillas á que queden muy untadas, después se les echa pan
rallado y se fríen en manteca que se haya quemado muy
bien, pero que no mas está tibia para que no se doren mu-
cho. Hágase otra salsa con jitomates codidos que se muelen
y bajan del metate con agua limpia; se aettrona un poco de
cebolla, se refríe mucho el jitomate con sal y un poco de
perejil muy menudo. Al llevarlas ó la mesa se les agrega
vino de Jerez.

excerpts.translation: 405. Ribs with pulque. — The ribs are tied to the mouth of a pot, into which a quart of pulque is poured for every six ribs, half a cup of sherry wine and the same amount of water, crushed garlic, Mexican thyme, and ground pepper. The pot is covered with a cloth. Make a sauce with a quart of milk and a handful of flour, and add it little by little as the ribs heat up so that they become very coated, then they are sprinkled with breadcrumbs and fried in lard that has been burned very well, but is only warm so that they do not brown too much. Make another sauce with ripe tomatoes that are ground and passed through the metate with clean water; a little onion is chopped, the tomato is fried with salt and a little very finely chopped parsley. When serving them on the table, sherry wine is added.

409. Sesos á la veracruxana. — Después de bien limpios se
ponen á cocer en agua y sal, se cortan en pequeñas rebana-
das y se bañan en el batido que de antemano estará hecho,
compuesto de tres huevos, manteca derretida, sal, núes
moscada, pimienta y pan rallado; se van friendo poco á po-
co, y cuando se vea están doraditos, se sacan y colocan en
un platón fécheseles con una cuchara un poco de salsa de
jitomate, clarita y plátanos fritos maduros.

Brain à la veracruxana. — After being well cleaned, they are put to cook in water and salt, cut into small slices, and dipped in the beaten mixture that has been prepared in advance, composed of three eggs, melted butter, salt, nutmeg, pepper, and breadcrumbs; they are fried little by little, and when they appear golden, they are removed and placed on a platter; with a spoon, a little clear tomato sauce and ripe fried plantains are poured over them.

421. Orejas de ternera/ritas. — Córtense á lo largo, en cua-
tro pedazos, orejas preparadas y cocidas. Pónganse en ado-
bo con vinagre, sal y pimienta en grano; rebócense en ma-
sa clara y f ríanse; extendiéndolas prontamente en la sartén
y dándolas vueltas; se escurren para servirlas cubiertas de
perejil frito. ^

422. Orejas de ternera á la italiana. — Después de limpias
y pasadas por la llama se escaldan y se ponen en agua fría;
cuezanse en agua ó en una cacerola cubierta de rebanadas
de tocino, con perejil, cebollas y algunas rajas de limón,
échese caldo de sustancias y buen vino blanco, cúbranse las
orejas oon otras lonjas de tocino, y por encima con papel
engrasado; al cabo de hora y media estarán cosidas: se sacan
y escurren, se sacan y se atan las puntas como si fuesen ce-
bollas; sírvanse con una salsa italiana.

423. Cabeza de ternera en salpican. — Escáldese para qui-
tarla el vello, póngase en agua fría para que suelte toda la
porquería, por espacio de veinticuatro horas, quítense los
huesos de la mandíbula inferior y el extremo del hocicó, no
dejando mas hueso que. el cráneo. Frótese oon limón y há-
gase cocer, envuelta en un paño, en agua sazonada con sal

ías

y pimienta, un manojo de perejil y yerbas, cebollas, zanaho-
rias, miga de pan y un puñado de harina. Cuando este* co-
cida ae saca, so deja escurrir; se quitan con cuidado los hue-
sos del cráneo; se descubren los sesos, y se sirve guarneci-
da de perejil y cebollas picadas. Cada uno la sazona en su
plato y ásu gusto, con sal, pimienta, aceite y vinagre.

424 Cabeza de ternera á la gallineta. — Prepárese y cue-
zase como la precedente. Hágase una gallineta, en la que
se echan los pedazos de cabeza antes de ligarla; hágase her-
vir lentamente un instante, ligúese con yemas de huevo sin
dejarlo cocer, y sírvase con zumo de limón.

425. Molleja de temeía, — Se lava en varias aguas y se
deja escaldar un cuarto de hora en agua hirviendo; después
se puede emplear en los guisos que se crea oportuno.

426. Molleja de ternera mechada. — Méchese con tiritas de
tocino la molleja después de preparada como queda dicho,
cuezase en el horno con una buena reducción por espacio
de tres cuartos de hora, báñese de un buen color y pónga-
se sobre acederas, ó en una salsa de jitomate.

421. Veal ears/ritas. — Cut lengthwise into four pieces, prepared and cooked ears. Place in a marinade with vinegar, salt, and whole peppercorns; coat in egg white batter and fry; spreading them quickly in the pan and turning them; drain to serve them covered with fried parsley. ^

422. Veal ears Italian style. — After cleaning and passing over the flame, they are scalded and placed in cold water; cook in water or in a saucepan covered with slices of bacon, with parsley, onions, and some lemon slices, add broth from substances and good white wine, cover the ears with other slices of bacon, and on top with greased paper; after an hour and a half they will be cooked: remove and drain, remove and tie the ends as if they were onions; serve with an Italian sauce.

423. Veal head in salpican. — Scald to remove the hair, place in cold water to release all the dirt, for twenty-four hours, remove the bones from the lower jaw and the end of the snout, leaving no bone other than the skull. Rub with lemon and cook, wrapped in a cloth, in water seasoned with salt and pepper, a bunch of parsley and herbs, onions, carrots, bread crumbs, and a handful of flour. When this is cooked, remove it, let it drain; carefully remove the bones from the skull; uncover the brains, and serve garnished with chopped parsley and onions. Each person seasons it on their plate and to their taste, with salt, pepper, oil, and vinegar.

424. Veal head à la gallineta. — Prepare and cook as the preceding one. Make a gallineta, into which the pieces of head are placed before binding it; let it simmer slowly for an instant, bind with egg yolks without letting it cook, and serve with lemon juice.

425. Veal gizzard. — Wash in several waters and let scald for a quarter of an hour in boiling water; afterwards it can be used in stews as deemed appropriate.

426. Larded veal gizzard. — Lard the gizzard with strips of bacon after preparing it as stated above, cook in the oven with a good reduction for three quarters of an hour, baste until a good color and place on sorrel, or in a tomato sauce.

449. Albóndigas de. te-mercu — Se muele media libra de ter-
nera y media de carne de puerco con pimienta y sal. Se
pica jitomate, cebolla y ajo muy roenudito y se fríe bien en
manteca. Cuezanse aparte unas papas y chorizos, y esto se
sancocha en el recaudo, añádase unas alcaparras, un huevo
cocido y un poco de porejil. Con la carne que ya está mo-
lida se hacen albóndigas en las cuales se echa un poco de
picadillo; f ríanse después en manteca. Hágase luego una
salsa con media cabeza de ajos fritos, tres jitomates gran-
des asados y molidos, y unas alcaparras. Se muele todo sin
quitarle los prietitos al jitomate y se fríe bien en manteca.
Ya que está se le echa el agua y luego las albóndigas, y se
deja cocer.
450. Otras albóndigas. — Se pica un poco de lomo de ter-
nera, se muele con unos gajos de cebolla, unos dientes de
ajo, especias finas y un poco de pan remojado; se le agrega
vinagre, poca cantidad, manteca y un huevo; se revuelve
bien y se hacen las albóndigas echándolas en la salsa si-
guiente: se pica cebolla menudita, se fríe en manteca y acei-
te: se muelen unos dos jitomates con especias finas y un pe-
dazo de pan frito; huevos cocidos con todo y clara, se incor-
poran con la cebolla y así que está todo frito se van echan-
do las albóndigas á que se cuezan, pero sin echarles agua,

449. Meatballs of. te-mercu — Half a pound of veal and half a pound of pork meat are ground with pepper and salt. Tomatoes, onions, and garlic are finely chopped and fried well in lard. Potatoes and chorizos are boiled separately, and this is simmered in the sauce; capers, a boiled egg, and a little parsley are added. With the ground meat, meatballs are made into which some chopped mixture is put; they are then fried in lard. A sauce is then made with half a head of fried garlic, three large roasted and ground tomatoes, and some capers. Everything is ground without removing the seeds from the tomatoes and is fried well in lard. Once it is ready, water is added and then the meatballs, and it is left to cook.

450. Other meatballs. — A little veal loin is chopped, ground with some onion wedges, some cloves of garlic, fine spices, and a little soaked bread; vinegar, a small amount, lard, and an egg are added; it is mixed well and the meatballs are made by putting them in the following sauce: onion is finely chopped, fried in lard and oil; about two tomatoes are ground with fine spices and a piece of fried bread; boiled eggs with everything including the white are incorporated with the onion and once everything is fried, the meatballs are added to cook, but without adding water,

451. Albóndigas de ternera. — Se pican y muelen pulpas
de ternera con sal y poca pimienta. Estando ya molido se
hace en el mismo metate una tortilla gorda y se le ponen
tiras de jamón y pimientas enteras, y se enrolla á modo de
chorizon. Se pone á cocer en una tortera con agua, vinagre
y vino de Jerez, laurel, tomillo, orégano, mejorana y unos
ajos enteros, cuidando que no se pegue. Ya que está coci-

451. Beef meatballs. — The pulp of beef is chopped and ground with salt and a little pepper. Once ground, a thick tortilla is made on the same metate, strips of ham and whole peppers are added to it, and it is rolled up like a chorizo. It is put to cook in a tortera with water, vinegar, and sherry wine, laurel, thyme, oregano, marjoram, and some whole garlic cloves, taking care that it does not stick. Once the meat is cooked, it is left to cool, sliced, and dressed with oil and vinegar, or a sauce of cooked tomatoes with whole young onions and ground garlic is made, all of which is fried.

452. Tongue. — Capers are fried, some tomatoes are roasted, everything is browned in lard, ground, and fried in lard and oil: then fine ground spices are added. Once this sauce is seasoned, the cooked and sliced tongue is added and left to rest.

rellenan con la cebolla y perejil, se polvorean con las especias las rebanadas de jamón y se ponen en los agujoros- Ya
que está claveteado todo el lomo se echa manteca en una

póngase luego el agua y cuando esté la carne cocida y el caldo espeso, rocíese con vino de Jerez y póngasele aceitunas.

delgado y se aplana como para bifteck, se les echa un poco
de vinagre y sal, y se dejan así. Media hora antes de comer se ponen á asar á la parrilla untándoles una poquita de
manteca á fuego muy manso, se voltea para que doren de
los dos lados, y la mante quita que escurre se les echa por
encima después de puestos en el platón. Al ponerlos á asar

484. Another stew. — Chop quite a bit of onion very finely and a little parsley, stir; cut strips of ham very thin, stir cloves, cinnamon and pepper; make deep holes in the loin with a knife and fill them with the onion and parsley, sprinkle the slices of ham with the spices and put them in the holes. Once the whole loin is studded, put butter in a casserole and put the loin in it to fry. Once fried, add quite a bit of ground tomato without the seeds and let it fry again; then add the water and when the meat is cooked and the broth thick, sprinkle with sherry wine and add olives.

485. Grilled loin, from Juitsita. — Slice the loin thin and flatten it like a steak, sprinkle with a little vinegar and salt, and leave it like that. Half an hour before eating, put it on the grill, brushing with a little butter over very low heat, turn it so that it browns on both sides, and the melted butter that drips off is poured over it after placing it on the platter. 489. Lomo de pobre — It is fried in lard and mixed with ground spices and a good portion of cooked tomatoes. The necessary water and salt are added, and once it is soft, it is left to dry, with a little Malaga wine added.

490. Guisado de ¿orno.— The loin is sliced into strips less than one finger wide, a lot of parsley, onion, and garlic are chopped, and put into a pot of water; oil, oregano, ground pepper, and raw ham are added; all this is fried with the loin. Roasted and ground tomatoes are prepared, fried in the same oil in which the meat and seasoning were fried, water with a little salt, oregano, thyme, crumbled laurel, and Castile vinegar are added; after it has boiled a few times, half a quart of Jerez wine is added, and if it thickens too much, more wine is poured in, but not water, because it curdles. It is garnished with lettuce, radishes, chilies, and olives.

602. Others with zucchini. — Chop solid meat and head* meat; once the meat is chopped, add two 6 ti es raw eggs and a little salt and pepper and grind well. Put butter in a casserole, two or three bunches of scallions, cut into wedges, one or two chopped tomatoes, parsley also chopped; once it is fried, add flour and let it fry all together; once it is fried, add water. Grind cloves, cinnamon, pepper and two or three cloves of garlic, make the meatballs and put them in the broth with whole zucchinis. Let it cook a little before serving.
603. Other meatballs. — Chop the loin and solid meat; put it in a casserole with two or three boiled eggs with salt, ground cloves, cinnamon and pepper, a little aged cheese grated, chopped onion and parsley, mix well, put it in a pan with butter, make the meatballs as is customary and fry them; put aside in a casserole the butter, chopped onion, garlic and one or two tomatoes and fry; toast almonds on a comal, grind them and put them to fry in the same casserole and add water; grind cloves, cinnamon, pepper and a piece of fried bread; a little chopped parsley and another of thyme. Let it boil and when it is thick, put the meatballs there, let it give a few boils and serve.

ja freir bien y después se rellenan oon esto unas rebanadas

excerpts.translation:
505. Asadura. — It is put to cook with thyme, marjoram and laurel. Onion and tomato are fried, but when the seasoning is well fried, a little bread is added to brown it, and it should not brown too much, along with the chopped offal, separating a few pieces to grind them with the spices and a clove of garlic. The ground mixture is stirred with an egg and also added when heating to go to the table, with a little oil, and the dish is garnished with chopped parsley, capers, boiled egg and fried bread.

When the offal has finished cooking, it is rinsed in warm water; the bread must be fried separately.

506. Pork offal. — It is cut into small pieces and put in water to degrease. A lot of onion, garlic, tomato and parsley are chopped, all very finely. It is put in a casserole with lard, all together, with pieces of ham and some pork ribs, and it is parboiled; oregano, powdered thyme and spices of ground cloves, cinnamon and cumin are added. Once it is fried, enough water is added to cook it, along with Castile vinegar; it can be left with broth or marinated. It is served with chili peppers in vinegar, olives and capers.

607. Loin casings. — Peas, green beans and string beans are put to cook; after they are cooked and chopped, they are fried in oil and lard with their salt, a pinch of pepper, a little cheese; when it is almost finished, it is fried well and then these are used to stuff slices of pork loin, which are tied with a thin string; to keep them tight and prevent the filling from coming out, they are put to cook in a little water with a small amount of salt; garlic cloves are also fried in lard and oil, which are ground with some roasted tomatoes; the seasoning is fried again until it cools down completely; then the meat is added to parboil with the seasoning, and once it is done, a little water is added to season it.

685. Gallina atada, — Móchese con lonjas de tocino, en-
vuélvase en un papel engrasado y póngase en el asador;
cuando esto casi asada se le quita el papel para que tome
color, se bañan las lonjas de tocino, si se puede se ooloca
sobre berros de fuente, expolvoreada de sal, con un poco de
vinagre y se sirve regada con jugo.

686. Pepitoria de gallina. — Se corta en trozos, escáldense
tres minutos en agua hirviendo, escúrranse y pónganse en
una cacerola con manteca, perejil en rama y cebollas peque-
ñas: rehogúese el todo, añádase una cucharada de' harina y
mójese con caldo, se sazona con sal y pimienta, hágase co-
cer, y después retírense los cuartos de gallina; redúzcase la
salsa, que se ouela, ligúese con yemas de huevo sin que hier"
va, y échese sobre los pedazos de gallina con zumo de limón.

687. Pepitoria de menudiüo* de gallina, etc. — Con los
alones» mollejas, crestas, pescuezos 6 higadillos se hace
ana pepitoria, friéndolas después en manteca con cebolla y
jitomate; luego se machacan ajos, pimienta, sal, clavillo,
canela y perejil; cnando están cocidos y menguada la salsa,
se echa salsa de avellanas, con la cual dará un hervor, y
después se pone un poco de ácido de limón.

688. Albondiguillas de gallina, etc. — Se tomarán las pe-
chugas y se picarán menudo con alguna gordura de gallina;
se mezclará con el picado pan en remojo y yemas de huevo
cocido, sal, pimienta y canela molidas; se bate todo en hue-
vo crudo dándole la suficiente consistencia; se hacen las al-
bondiguillas redondas, empanándolas al rededor, y después
de fritas se cuecen en sustancia de aves y se echa salsa
blanca.

689. Gallina en pebre. —Estando limpia y sin vientre, se
pone á asar en unas parrillas, untando muy á menudo con
manteca derretida, sumo de limón, sal y ajos machacados;
estando medio asada, se pone en una cazuela, echando man.
teca, perejil picado, pimienta, sal, dos 6 tres hojas de lau-
rel, el unto 6 manteca que sobró del asado, media taza de
aceite crudo y la agua suficiente hasta cubrirla; se deja que
hierva hasta que está blanda, se saca la gallina, deslíense
en él caldo ocho yemas de huevos, batiéndolas bien para
que espese el caldo; se \e deja hervir un poco, y se echa por
encima de la gallina, que estará en un platón, y se sirve.

685. Hen tied, — Place slices of bacon, wrap in greased paper and put on the spit; when this is almost roasted, remove the paper so that it takes color, bathe the slices of bacon, if possible place on watercress, dusted with salt, with a little vinegar and serve with juice.

686. Hen pepitoria. — Cut into pieces, scald for three minutes in boiling water, drain and put in a saucepan with butter, parsley in sprigs and small onions: sauté everything, add a spoonful of flour and moisten with broth, season with salt and pepper, let cook, and then remove the quarters of hen; reduce the sauce, which is [illegible], thicken with egg yolks without boiling, and pour over the pieces of hen with lemon juice.

218

687. Pepitoria of chicken offal, etc. — With wings, gizzards, crests, necks or livers, make a pepitoria, frying them afterwards in butter with onion and tomato; then crush garlic, pepper, salt, clove, cinnamon and parsley; when they are cooked and the sauce reduced, add hazelnut sauce, with which it will boil, and then add a little lemon acid.

688. Small chicken meatballs, etc. — Take the breasts and chop finely with some chicken fat; mix with chopped soaked bread and cooked egg yolks, salt, pepper and ground cinnamon; beat everything in raw egg giving it sufficient consistency; make the meatballs round, breading them around, and after frying, cook in poultry stock and add white sauce.

689. Hen in pebre. — Being clean and without belly, put to roast on grates, brushing very often with melted butter, lemon juice, salt and crushed garlic; when half roasted, put in a casserole, adding butter, chopped parsley, pepper, salt, two or three leaves of laurel, the fat or butter that remained from roasting, half a cup of raw oil and enough water to cover it; let it boil until it is soft, remove the hen, dissolve in the broth eight egg yolks, beating them well to thicken the broth; let it boil a little, and pour over the hen, which will be on a platter, and serve.

701. Relleno para gallina. — Se pican unos dientes de ajo
menuditos, se pone un poco de manteca y agua en una ca-
zuela y allí se pone á freír hasta que sé consuma el agua.
Se fríen seis criadillas, con una taza de cebolla picada, me-
dia taza de tomates lavados y picados para que se les caigan
las pepitas. Estando ya fritos se pican las criadillas y se
echan en el recaudo con una cucharada del caldo en que se
cocieron. Se le echa clavo, pimienta y canela todo molido,
un poco de perejil picado, tomillo, jamón cocido en reba-
nadas, alcaparras, aceitunas y un poco de aceite.

Six criadillas are fried, with a cup of chopped onion, half a cup of tomatoes washed and chopped so that their seeds fall off. Once fried, the criadillas are chopped and put into the sauce with a spoonful of the broth in which they were cooked. Clove, pepper, and cinnamon, all ground, a little chopped parsley, thyme, cooked ham in slices, capers, olives, and a little oil are added to it.

mo y jamón, todo crudo, asi se alterna hasta llenar la ca-

tes, jitomates, y se echa al caldillo clavo, canela, pimienta
y un poco de culantro, y ya que está bien sazonado, se le
echa vinagre, pedazos de pina, ajonjolí, aceitunas, chiles y
azafrán.

adorna con chiles y alcaparras.

707. Gallinas gachupinas. — Take some hens and some raw loins; the former are cut into quarters and the latter are sliced with onions, tomatoes, garlic and pineapple; grease a casserole with lard, and put in a layer of the aforementioned seasoning, adding parsley to it, on top another layer of hen, loin and ham, all raw, thus alternating until the casserole is full; to each layer sprinkle a powder of cloves, cinnamon, plenty of pepper and vinegar; place the casserole over two fires until it is well seasoned; garnish the dish with pine nuts, raisins, almonds, capers, chilies, olives, citron and oil.

706. Gallinas cautivas. — Boil and chop in the broth gizzards, sweetbreads, chorizo, ham and then grind sweet potatoes, tomatoes, and add to the broth cloves, cinnamon, pepper and a little coriander, and once it is well seasoned, add vinegar, pieces of pineapple, sesame seeds, olives, chilies and saffron.

709. Gallina en espinaca. — Boil the hens with loins, ham and chorizo; put spinach and chickpeas to cook, cut the hens into pieces, fry separately tomatoes, garlic and green chilies and add to them the well-squeezed spinach and chickpeas, then the meat; add raisins, almonds, citron, hard-boiled eggs, sliced banana, a little vinegar, sweet potatoes, saffron and all spices. Once it is well seasoned separately, pour oil over it and garnish with chilies and capers.

excerpts.translation: 854. Robalo with jitomate. — The robalo is desalted and then, after drying it with a napkin, it is fried in lard and oil. A good amount of jitomate without seeds, three bunches of onion, and one head of garlic are chopped, all very finely, along with a good amount of parsley, chopping each ingredient separately. Oil and lard are added to a casserole. The garlic is fried first, then the onion, and then the jitomate with the parsley; this last ingredient is fried thoroughly. A little thyme is added, and cloves, pepper, cinnamon, and saffron are ground; a little water and vinegar are left to boil until thickened, some capers are added, and the fish is put in to boil over low heat. Add a good amount of oil, and to serve it on the table, garnish with chiles, capers, and olives.

861. Pickled catfish. — It is washed very well with lemon, and once it is clean it is dried with a napkin, it is coated with flour, it is fried with plenty of oil and lard and a layer of fish is placed in a pot and on top a layer of the lard in which it was fried, on top of which cloves and ground pepper and some leaves of laurel, orange tree, oregano and thyme are added. The pot is filled with vinegar, which should be half creole and the other half from Castile, with oil. The pot is covered and left for three days, after which the catfish is taken out and placed on a platter to serve it.

Parsley is chopped and added to the dish along with a little vinegar and breadcrumbs.

882. Ostiones. — Se pica menudo mucho jitomate, cebolla
y perejil; se emplea para una lata de ostiones dos onzas de
mantequilla que se pone á freír; cuando está quemada se le
incorpora medio cuartillo de aceite español; ya que está muy
caliente se fríe en esa mezcla el recaudo, al cual se añadirán
muchas alcaparras y aceitunas; estando todo frito échense
los ostiones con sal si les faltare y déjese á fuego manso á
que espese.

pués se sacan del agua; se enjugan y se les quita la hueva;
se echan .en una sartén aceite y manteca y se fríen las moja-
rras con mucho cuidado procurando que no se partan; en la
misma manteca en que se frieron se fríen las huevas después
de partidas en rebanadas muy delgaditas, se sacan y en la
misma manteca se fríen rebanadas 4c pan; se sacan éstas y

se frió junto con el pan, échese con el jitomate y la cebo-
lla, añádase un polvo de pimienta, un poco de vinagre y

echando sobre ellas lo que sobre cuando se hayan puesto
ya en el platón. Agregúese al pescado el resto de las huevas
rebanadas junto con rebanadas de pan frito. Recomenda-

mates, cebolla y perejil también picados. Se muelen cla-
vos» canela, pimienta y cominos. Se echa un poco de agua

888. Mojarra with their roe** — They are washed very well; then they are taken out of the water; they are dried and their roe is removed;
oil and butter are put in a frying pan and the mojarra are fried with great care, taking care that they do not break; in

the same butter, slices of bread are fried; these are taken out and
always in the same butter, chopped tomatoes and
very finely chopped onion are fried. Half of the fried roe is ground together with the bread, it is added with the tomato and onion, a pinch of pepper is added, a little vinegar and
a good amount of oil; it is left to simmer and when it is
ready, the mojarra are soaked with this sauce inside and out,
pouring over them what remains when they have already been placed
on the platter. The rest of the sliced roe is added to the fish along with slices of fried bread. We recommend this dish.

889. Other mojarra» — They are cleaned and fried in butter until golden. Having done this, they are removed from the heat and many finely chopped garlic cloves are fried; then tomatoes, onion and parsley, also chopped, are fried. Cloves, cinnamon, pepper and cumin are ground. A little water is added

para freirías se revuelcan en harina; se fríen en aceite y
manteca. Se asan tres 6 cuatro jitomates y se muelen con

también se echa el huevo bien picado, un poco de perejil y
pimienta en polvo; este relleno ha de quedar seco; se relle-
nan los pámpanos y se cosen con una hebra, se pone una
sartén con manteca y aceite y allí se fríen los pámpanos en-
teros sin quitarles las colas ni nada; se ponen á asar unos
jitomates, se muele junto con un poco de perejil fresco, un
poco de orégano y tomillo; esto se fríe donde se frieron los

te, ya que está bien frito, se le echa una poca de agua, se
muele clavo, canela, pimienta y se le eoha; se ponen los
pámpanos en una sartén ó tortera donde quepan enteros y

890. Mojarra*. — Cleaned and washed, they are dried whole and, to fry them, they are rolled in flour; they are fried in oil and butter. Three or four tomatoes are roasted and ground with capers, fresh parsley, one head of peeled garlic and the necessary salt. The mojarra are placed on a platter and bathed with this sauce. Chiles, olives, capers and plenty of oil are added and they are put to cook over gentle heat. Any other fish may be cooked in this sauce.

891. Stuffed grape leaf*. — The grape leaf is put to soak; once desalted, it is dried in a cloth; some eggs are put to cook; once they are well cooked, they are peeled and chopped into large pieces; a little onion and tomato are chopped, fried in oil and butter and fried very well; also the well-chopped egg, a little parsley and powdered pepper are added; this stuffing must remain dry; the grape leaves are stuffed and sewn with a thread, a pan with butter and oil is placed and there the whole grape leaves are fried without removing their tails or anything; some tomatoes are roasted, ground together with a little fresh parsley, a little oregano and thyme; this is fried where the grape leaves were fried, some onion wedges and plenty of oil are added, once it is well fried, a little water is added, cloves, cinnamon and pepper are ground and added to it; the grape leaves are placed in a pan or skillet where they fit whole and

370

spread out, this sauce which must remain thick is poured over it and it is garnished with chile, caper and caper berries.

892. Another stuffed grape leaf*. — The grape leaf is detached, and dried, taking care that it is not perforated, a little tomato without seeds and a little onion and garlic with a little parsley are chopped; once it is parboiled, the parsley and tomato are added to be fried well and everything must be fried in oil and butter; a little pepper and thyme are added, once everything has been fried well, capers, olives, strips of chile in vinegar, almonds, raisins and some strips of boiled egg are added and with all the aforementioned the fish is stuffed, taking care that it remains tight; it is sewn with a thick thread, a pan is lined with oil and butter and there the grape leaf is put to fry, it is turned carefully to one side so that it does not fall apart, and it remains well fried on both sides; it is removed from the heat and left in the same vessel.

excerpts.raw:
896. Otro.— Se fríen en manteca dos chiles mulatos y se
muelen con la misma; se fríe ajo á que quede trasparente,
cebolla y jitomate; so echa el chile, un pedazo de pan frito
y molido para que espese y se pone el pescado en esta salsa.

897. lAaa fría. —Se lava bien y se cuece. Se hacen her-
vir jitomates enteros y cebollas enteras también, que se
mezclan después de quitar á los jitomates el pellejo; se le
añade orégano y pimienta en polvo, sal, aceitunas, un pu-
ñado de alcaparras y aceite. Al ir á servir el pescado se em-
barra con esta salsa. Se adorna con aguacate y tornachiles.

898. lÁta atada. — Se pica un manojo de cebolla con tres
cabezas de ajos muy menudos; se echa uncuartillo de aceite
en una cazuela y se fríe lo picado agregando orégano, to-
millo, clavo y pimienta, el jugo de un limón, un puñado de
alcaparras /sal Se embarra una tortera de manteca, y se
cubre el fondo de jitomates y cebollas rebanadas. Se hacen
unas incisiones á lo largo de las lisas por ambos lados y ya
que están preparadas se colocan sobre la capa de cebolla y
manteca que están en la tortera, y se cubren después con
todo el recaudo anterior. Se pone la tortera en la lumbre y
se tapa con un comal con bastante lumbre por encima. Ha
de quedar con muy poco caldo y como asado. Se le echa
por encima aceite y chiles en vinagre. *

272

y ae lea quita la cáacsra. Se pica media caben de ajo muy
menudita, un poco de jitomate sin pepitas, un poco de ce-
bolla y perejil. Se frie en aceite y manteca el ajo y la ce-
bolla, ae le echa un poco de tomillo, tal, claro, canela y pi-
mienta con unas hebraa de azafrán, todo molida Ya que
está frito ae echa en el recaudo loa camarones y chiles, acei-
tunas y Alcaparras.
900. Camarones frescos. — Ya limpios los camaronea ae po-
nen á oocer con un poco de sal, se fríen en aceite, se les
echa pan rallado, pimienta y clavo, unas gotas de limón y
papaa cocidas y partidas. Póngasele el agua suficiente y dé-
jense hervir; la salsa no debe quedar ni espesa ni aguada.

901. Quito de camaronee. — Calzase un poco de manteca;
cuando este* agregúesele un poco de aceite francés, bastan-
te cebolla bien picada, perejil, ajo y jitomate: ya bien frito
el recaudo se echan en él los camarones con aceitunas, alca-
parras, pimienta molida, pan remojado y un poco de vina-
gre, dejándolos sazonar con sal y procurando quede salaita.

excerpts.translation: 908. Another fish. —Oil and 7 manteen are heated, one head of garlic is finely chopped and fried until it browns; in this state, half a tasa of chopped onion is fried, a little chopped parsley, two or three peeled jitomates, split chilchotes: when the manteca begins to separate, a little ground clove and cumin are added, half a wide or mulato chile, and a slice of fried bread ground. Once fried, the fish is added

excerpts.raw:
909. Pescado á la minuta, — Limpio y hecho pedazos el
pescado, se le quitan las espinas, se sala y se deja escurrir
y se deja así tres 6 cuatro horas. Una antes de comer-
lo se pone en zumo de limón con orégano. Se baten hue-
vos con polvos de galleta y no se deja cuajar, se revuelca
el pescado en esta salsa y se fríe en aceite y manteca.
910. Pescado en salsa amarilla. — Poco antes de servir la
comida, se pone en la lumbre una cazuela con aceite y man-
teca en cantidad igual y en proporción á la cantidad de pes-
cado. En cuanto hierva se le echan jitomates, pimientas,
ajos y cebollas todo muy picado. Cuando está frito se le
echa agua á que cubra el pescado; cuando hierve mucho se
sazona con clavo, pimienta negra y pimienta de Tabasco to-
do molido. Entonces se pone el pescado en el caldo á que
se cueza. Se le añade azafrán molido hasta que tome un
color amarillo claro. Se coje una torta de pan, que debe
haberse puesto en remojo desde antes y se remuele con
salsa del pescado; se agrega el pan al guiso y se deja freír
para que no quede crudo.

excerpts.translation:
909. Minced fish. — The fish, cleaned and cut into pieces, is deboned, salted, and left to drain, and thus left for three or four hours. One hour before eating it, it is placed in lemon juice with oregano. Eggs are beaten with cracker crumbs and not allowed to set; the fish is rolled in this sauce and fried in oil and butter.

910. Fish in yellow sauce. — Shortly before serving the meal, a pot is placed on the fire with oil and butter in equal amounts and in proportion to the quantity of fish. As soon as it boils, tomatoes, peppers, garlic, and onions, all very finely chopped, are added. When it is fried, water is added to cover the fish; when it boils vigorously, it is seasoned with ground cloves, black pepper, and Tabasco pepper. Then the fish is placed in the broth to cook. Ground saffron is added until it takes a light yellow color. A piece of bread, which should have been soaked beforehand, is taken and mixed with the fish sauce; the bread is added to the stew and fried until it is no longer raw.

excerpts.raw:
912. Otro con jitomate. — Para seis libras de pescado se
ponen veinte jitomates grandes molidos con bastantes ajos
también molidos, estos últimos se fríen aparte á que se
quemen en aceite español y manteca; ya que estén se lee
echan los jitomates molidos, y al romper el hervor se van
metiendo en la cazuela las rebanadas de pescado, después
de haberle escamado y secado bien con un trapo. 8e echa
la sal pimienta molida, chiles en vinagre, aceitunas, alca-

vinagre, colocándolo al borde de la hornilla; se quiebran en
ella los huevos sin reventar los, siempre hirviendo el agua,
se dejan cuajar, se retiran con una cuchara agujerada, y si
tienen alguna consistencia se meten en agua fría. Se les
cambia el agua, y un poco antes de servirlos se calientan,
se enjugan sobre un lienzo blanco y se ponen en un píate,
echando encima de cada huevo un polvo de pimienta, una
gota de vinagre ó* zumo de limón.
1.005. Huevos con jitomate*. — Se fríe primero la manteca
ó* aceite, después los jitomates muy pica ditos, y si se quiere,
antes un poco de cebolla también picada. Se echan los huevos perfectamente batidos y se revuelven con el jitomate,
pudiendo servirse como una tortilla, y si tienen pedazos de
jamón, formarán un buen plato de almuerzo.
excerpts.translation:
1.004. Fried eggs with «alto». — Fill three quarters of the pot with water and a little vinegar, placing it on the edge of the stove; break the eggs into it without breaking them, always with the water boiling, let them set, remove with a slotted spoon, and if they have some consistency, put them in cold water. Change the water, and just before serving, warm them, dry them on a white cloth, and place them on a plate, sprinkling each egg with a powder of pepper, a drop of vinegar or lemon juice.

1.005. Eggs with jitomate*. — First fry the butter or oil, then the very finely chopped jitomates, and if desired, a little chopped onion beforehand. Add the perfectly beaten eggs and stir with the jitomate, which can be served as an omelette, and if they have pieces of ham, they will make a good lunch dish.

excerpts.raw:
1.022. Huevos duros. -Cuezanse con cascara 7 cuando es-
tén duros se sacan 7 se les quita aquella; córtense en rue-
das, 7 puestas en un plato se sirven con sal, aceite, vinagre
7 pimienta.

Suelen servirse de este modo para adornar ensaladas cru-
das, platos de espárragos, coliflores, etc.

1.023. Huevos revueltos con jitomate. — Frianse los jitoma-
tes 7 después de sazonados se echan los huevos bien bati-
dos, proporcionando su cantidad, 7 revuélvase todo hasta
que estén bien cuajados.

1.024. Huevos con cebolla. — Se ponen del mismo modo
que los anteriores, 7 añadiéndoles un poco de calabacín pi-
cado, se formará lo que suele llamarse pisto.

1,026. Huevos escalfados. — Se unta un plato hondo con
manteca, expolvoreándolo con un poco de sal; pónganse en*
cima los huevos: deslíase un poco de manteca con una cu-
charada de leche ó nata, 7 cuando esto bien caliente se
echa por encima, se tapa bien poniendo el plato á fuego
lento, 7 se sirve.

1,026. Huevos rellenos guisado». — Se endurecen los hue-

309

▼os y se parten en dos mitades, se sacan las yemas y se
muelen con miga de pan mojada en crema; añádase una
parte igual de manteca, una 6 dos yemas, sal y pimienta.
Con este conjunto se rellenan los hueToe y se les cubre con
miga de pan humedecida con mantees; se echa el resto del
relleno, que se deslíe con un poco de caldo y se deja que de*
un hervor; también se rellenan con pescado picado y se usa
aceite.

1.027. Huevos con perejil. —En una vasija ancha se pone
perejil, ajos fritos, asafran, sal, pimienta, una hoja de yer-
babuena y yerbas finas, todo en rama; se echan los huevos
estrellados, se hace que d¿ un hervor, y se sacan con una
espumadera grande.

1.028. Huevos con leche,— A la manteca desleída se aña-
dirá perejil muy picado, sal y pimienta y un vaso de nata,
en la cual se haya desleído de antemano una cucharada de
harina. Cuando la salsa esté en punto se ponen en ella los
huevos cocidos hechos ruedas.

1.029. De otro modo. — Se deslíen seis huevos con dos on-
eas de azúcar, una cucharada de flor de naranja y un cuar-
tillo de leche; se pone esto en la vasija 6 plato muy hondo
en que se ha de servir, se deja cocer tres cuartos de hora en
el baño de María, se polvorea con azúcar muy fina y des-
pués se pasa por encima la plancha hecha ascua, y puede
servirse frío ó caliente.
1.030. Huevos en espuma, — Por cada media docena de
claras de huevo se tomarán dos onzas de azúcar rosada y se
batirán hasta que haga mucha espuma; se tendrá á calentar
en un cazo 6 cazuela nueva leche de cabras ú ovejas, y cuan-
do esté caliente se echa á cucharadas aquella espuma á co-

310

oer un poco, 7 luego ae sao* oon una espumadera para que
escurra la leche, y ae polvorea con canela.

1.031. Huevos fritos. —Póngase á freír aceite 7 cuando
esté' bien rujíente échese en él el huevo, 7 con una cucha-
ra de hierro plana salpíquese el aceite por encima para que
ae cubra la yema; sazóneseles oon sal molida 7 se sirve;
friendo uno á uno salen mejor.

1.032. De otro modo. — Luego que la manteca ó aceite es-
tá en su punto se estrellan 7 echan uno después de otro, 7
ouando están fritos se sirven oon sal por encima ó oon un
poco de jitomate, jamón ó acederas; generalmente salen
mejor fritos en cazuela que en sartén, porque en esta últi-
ma se arrebatan 7 pierden mucho.

LEGUMBRES.

1.033. Papas á la parisiense. — Póngase en una cacerola
un pedazo de manteca oon una cebolla muy picada; y déje-
sele freir hasta que tome un buen color.

Échese un vaso de agua y las papas mondadas oon pimien-
ta, sal, un ramito compuesto de yerbabuena, perejil, estra-
gón, etc., dejando que oueza todo poco á poco, y antes de
servir este guiso se quita dicho ramito.

1.034. Papas cocidas al vapor. — Se ponen las papas á 00-
oer enteras en una olla de barro ó cobre, en la que se echa
un poco de agua, y sobre la tapadera se pone un lienzo para
evitar la evaporación. De este modo son menos acres que
cocidas de otra manera.

1,036. Popas á la Naneta.— Hágase en la cacerola una

311

masa de buen color con mantequilla y harina, desliase con
caldo de carne ó de vigilia; échense las papas crudas, pela-
das y en pedazos delgados; añádase sal, pimienta, perejil en
rama y demás yerbas. Se pueden servir solas ó con la car-
ne asada que convenga.

1.036. Papas á la alemana, — Pélense y pártanse en reba-
nadas las papas cocidas en estofado, córtense pedacitos de
pan delgados y cuadrados, f ríase todo en mantequilla, pón-
gase en un plato hondo y riégúese con un cocido de harina
de papas. Antes de servirlas se puede dar color al guiso ro-
dándolo con asdcur y poniéndolo en el horno de campana.
También se puede dorar con una plancha hecha ascua.

1.062. Papas relimas.— Se pelan en crudo y se les hace
un agujerito para rellenarlas. El relleno se hace de sesos
cocidos y picados, fritos en aceite con un poco de perejil pi*
cado, pan rallado y un polvo de pimienta. Se les vuelve á
poner la tapa y se les da un ligero hervor en un poco de
agua, en un trasto extendido; para la salsa se asan unos ji«
tomates y con un pedazo de pan frito se muelen, se ponen
en una cazuela en la que se han frito antes unos gajo» de ce-
bolla, los jitomates y el pan; ya que está todo muy frito,
se le echa un poco de caldo de carne de puerco, especias
molidas y un poco de tomillo deshojado, se deja espesar
mucho y de este caldo se van bañando las papas rellenas,
se pone en una hornilla nada roas caliente, y encima una
lata con lumbre.

1.063. Arroz. — El arroz puede hacerse con pollos, pie*s de
cerdo, morcilla, salchicha, pájaros, lomo, carne, bacalao,
etc. Suponiendo que se hace con costillas, se dispondrá del
modo siguiente: se cuecen éstas con sal, luego se ponen á
freír con aceite, ajos, parejil, jitomate, un poquito de cebo-
lla, pimienta y jamón. El arroz en seco se restrega en un pa-
ño para que suelte el polvo y se echa en la cazuela meneán-
dolo; se echa el agua, teniendo presenta que cada pocilio de
arroz embebe sobre dos y medio de agua; añádase un polvo
de pimienta y clavo, y se deja á la lumbre hasta que quede
cocido y entero el grano. Se aparta de la lumbre y se cu-
bre con una cobertera con rescoldo.

1.062. Relimed potatoes.— They are peeled raw and a small hole is made in them to be stuffed. The stuffing is made of boiled and chopped brains, fried in oil with a little chopped parsley, breadcrumbs and a pinch of pepper. The lid is put back on them and they are given a light boil in a little water, in a wide vessel; for the sauce, some tomatoes are roasted and with a piece of fried bread they are ground, placed in a saucepan in which some slices of onion have been fried beforehand, the tomatoes and the bread; once everything is very fried, a little pork broth, ground spices and a little thyme leaves are added, it is left to thicken greatly and from this broth the stuffed potatoes are bathed, they are placed on a stove not too hot, and on top a tin with fire.

1.063. Rice.— Rice can be made with chickens, pig’s feet, blood sausage, sausage, birds, loin, meat, cod, etc. Assuming that it is made with ribs, it will be prepared as follows: these are boiled with salt, then they are fried with oil, garlic, parsley, tomato, a little onion, pepper and ham. The dry rice is rubbed in a cloth so that it releases the dust and is put in the saucepan stirring it; water is added, keeping in mind that each small measure of rice absorbs about two and a half measures of water; a pinch of pepper and cloves is added, and it is left on the fire until it is cooked and the grain is whole. It is removed from the fire and covered with a lid with embers.

arroz, como para hacer un pastel; pero en lugar de meterlo
en el molde, háganse las pelotillas, que se empapan en hue-
vos batidos con azúcar. Empánense con pan rallado; vuél-
vanse á empapar en huevo y á empanar en el pan rallado
por segunda vez y fríanse.
1.068. Arroz con polla*, — Se limpian y cortan en peda*
sos tres ó* cuatro pollos, se fríen bien en sartén 6 en cazue-
la de barro, con manteca, se los aumenta uno 6 dos dientes
de ajo, jitomate, perejil, alcachofas y ohí charos; se rehoga
todo bien, se aumenta un poco de chile huauchinango, pi-
mienta, clavo y un poco de azafrán, se pone el arroz y des*
pues de dos vueltas se cubre bien con caldo, y se hace co-
cer á grande fuego por el orden anterior.

Se puede hacer con gallinas, perdices, etc. ; mas cuando
sean aves duras 6 carnes, no se pondrá el arroz sino después
que están cocidas.

1.069. Arroz con bacalao seco. — Se toma como una libra
de bacalao seco, se tuesta al fuego, y cuando blandea se des-
hace menudo, quitándole las espinas, y luego se lava por

ajo, jitomate y perejil; cuando está frito se aumenta el ba-
calao bien escurrido; chile del tiempo, azafrán, pimienta y
clavo, se echa el arroz, se le da dos vueltas, y luego el agua
caliente, y se cuece como los anteriores. También puede
ponárscle chiles fritos 6 asados y mondados.

1,067* Arroz en croquetas, — Prepare a quarter of rice, as if making a pie; but instead of putting it in the mold, make the little balls, which are soaked in beaten eggs with sugar. Bread them with breadcrumbs; turn them again to soak in egg and bread with breadcrumbs a second time and fry.

1.068. Arroz con polla*, — Clean and cut into pieces three or four chickens, fry well in a pan or earthenware pot with butter, add one or two cloves of garlic, tomato, parsley, artichokes and ohí charos; sauté everything well, add a little chile huauchinango, pepper, clove and a little saffron, add the rice and after two turns cover well with broth, and cook over high heat in the previous order.

It can be made with hens, partridges, etc.; but when they are tough birds or meats, the rice will not be added until they are cooked.

1.069. Arroz con bacalao seco. — Take about one pound of dried cod, toast over the fire, and when soft, shred finely, removing the bones, and then wash with two cold waters. Place a pan, casserole or saucepan on the fire with oil, in which two or three cloves of garlic, tomato and parsley are fried; when fried, add the well-drained cod; chile of the season, saffron, pepper and clove, add the rice, give two turns, and then hot water, and cook as the previous ones. It can also have fried or roasted and peeled chiles added.

1.089. Sauce for stewing them. — A little garlic and a little onion, both things very finely chopped, a little tomato without seeds, fresh chopped parsley, butter and oil are put in a frying pan and the garlic is fried, then the onion, both things parboiled and on top the tomato with the parsley; this is fried a lot, a little water and salt, ground pepper, thyme are added; once seasoned, a little oil and vinegar are added, it is taken off the heat and in a tortera the artichokes are set upright, and with a spoon the sauce is poured over them and more oil; they are put on two slow fires so that they do not burn; the tortera is shaken at every moment, care is taken that the fire above it is small so that the artichokes do not brown; the broth should be thick, and it is served.

1.106. Col rellena para vitualla. — Se toma una col grande
y muy blanca, se le quitan los troncos y primeras hojas, se
cala por encima como sandia, esta cala se amarra con un
oordelito, se toma una olla proporcionada á la col, para que
no se desbarate, agua bastante, sal, ajos machacados, una
cascarita de tequezquite blanco, chiquita, y ya que esta hir-
viendo el agua en la olla, se echa la col á que se cueza, ya
que lo está, se saca con mucho cuidado para que no se des-
barate, se quita la cala y se rellena con lo siguiente: se fríe
un jitomate picado, cebolla, un poco de perejil, unos gar-
banzos cocidos en el puchero, un poco de caldo para que
cueza y se sazona, se le echa jamón, chorizo, ohorizones,
longaniza, peritas, todo esto rebanado, unos chícharos y
habas verdes también cocidas, antes de rellenar la col se
sazona todo lo dicho: *e pone una cazuela 6 sartén en que
quepa la col y se fríe con un poco de chile ancho remojado,
ajos y cominos, un poco de caldo del puchero y en esta
salsa se mete la col bañándola con una cuchara por enci-
ma, y á fuego manso, se sazona hasta que seque, procu-
rando que no quede salada ni desabrida y entera se lleva
caliente á la mesa para que se sirva.

nes y chorioitos, todo esto se sazona con las coles y para

1.106. Stuffed cabbage for provisions. — Take a large and very white cabbage, remove the stalks and first leaves, hollow it out from above like a watermelon, this hollowing is tied with a very thin thread, take a pot proportionate to the cabbage, so that it does not fall apart, enough water, salt, crushed garlic, a small piece of white tequezquite, and when the water in the pot is boiling, put the cabbage in to cook, when it is cooked, take it out with great care so that it does not fall apart, remove the hollowing and fill it with the following: fry a chopped tomato, onion, a little parsley, some chickpeas cooked in the pot, a little broth to cook and season, add ham, chorizo, large onions, longaniza, pears, all this sliced, some peas and green beans also cooked, before stuffing the cabbage, season all the above: * place a casserole or frying pan in which the cabbage fits and fry with a little soaked ancho chili, garlic and cumin, a little broth from the pot and in this sauce put the cabbage, basting it with a spoon from above, and over low heat, season until it dries, taking care that it does not remain salty or bland and whole it is taken hot to the table to be served.

1.107. Stuffed cabbages like for chiles. — Remove the crowns and put them back, tie them so that they do not fall apart and place them in a casserole so that they are well covered with water with its salt: when they are cooked, place them to drain, make the adobo and then open the cabbages leaf by leaf, and thread them and put [illegible] picadillo and the greater part is put in the center, when they are well stuffed, the leaves are gathered and tied.

1.108. Pickled cabbages. — Chop the cabbages and place them to cook with salt, when they have boiled a little, remove this water and add another hot one so that they finish cooking with more salt, place the mountain range to parboil, and there also add chopped tomato and a few whole onions: when this is parboiled, take it out and place it to drain, chop very finely and put it back with more tomato where the other is, when this is very well fried, wash the cabbages with another hot water and put them in the casserole with corresponding hot water and add a little laurel, thyme, oregano and the onions that were fried first, some heads of garlic, loose pepper, and a little oil and vinegar to taste, and the already cooked ham is added in slices, with large chorizos and small chorizos, all this is seasoned with the cabbages and to take to the table, garnish with chilies and olives.

de vinagre ó de agraz, y aun mejor zumo de limou.

1.169. Frijoles blanco* á la romana. — Córtense cebollas
en rebanadas y se rehogan en aceite, échense los frijoles
con perejil picado, sal y pimienta, y después que haya todo
cocido un rato, se ponen en un plato, y sobre ellos échese
un poco de vinagro hervido antes en cazuela.

1.170. Frijol** blancos.— *Se cuecen los frijoles blancos
con un poquito de agua de tequesquite; cuando están coci-
dos se lavan mucho, lo mismo que la olla en que se cocie-
ron: en la misma se eclia agua limpia, manteca y sal, se po-
ne á la lumbre, se pica bastante jitomate sin pepita y un
poco de cebolla, se echa bastante manteca en una cazuela,
se hace freír la cebolla, luego el jitomate y en seguida los
frijoles, se dejan hervir hasta que espesen para servirlos
con aceite, chiles en vinagre, etc.

1.171. Frijoles prietos. — Se cuecen sin tequesquite los fri-
joles prietos, después de cocidos se vacian en una cazuela;
se toma una sartén ó cazuela y se fríen con bastante man-
teca y todo recaudo de cocina, se les muele clavo y canela,
chiles, aceitunas, chorizos, longaniza y un poquito de vi-
nagre.

1.172. Otros frijoles bayos. — Después de cocidos se lavan
y se Jes echa una poca de cebolla frita, chile colorado molí-

344

do, unos pedazos de pichón y otrot de pechuga de gallina;
han de quedar cargaditos de manteca, después se les echa
un poco de riño de Jerez.

1.173. Lenteja» á la ama de cata. — Cuezanse las lentejas
en agua un poco salada, escúrranse y pónganse en una ca-
cerola con un buen pedazo de manteca, perejil picado, sal
y pimienta ; saltéense algunos minutos. Pónganse en el pla-
tón, adornándolas con cortezas de pan frito, y sírvanse muy
calientes.
1.174. Lenteja» á la mata* — Háganse enrojecer pedazos
de cebolla y yerbas finas picadas en mantequilla: añádase
harina; cuando la masa esté hecha, mójese con agua, y aun
mejor con caldo, échense en ello las lentejas cocidas en agua
y escurridas como las anteriores; añádase sal y pimienta,
saltéense lo mismo y sírvanse.

1.175. Lenteja» con tocino á la aldeana. — Pónganse lente-
jas y un buen pedazo de jamón en una olla llena de agua,
háganse cocer; cuando estén guísense como las anteriores y
pónganse en el platón sobre el jamón en que se han cocido.

1.176. Lenteja» con perejil — Se cuecen en agua y sal, se
escurren y ponen después en una cacerola con manteca abun-
dante, perejil picado, sal y un poco de pimienta, rehogúese
algunos minutos y se sirven con cortezas de pan frito, todo
muy caliente.

1.177. Lenteja». — Se ponen á cocer, y ya que están coci-
das se pica bastante jitomate, cebolla y ajo; se fríe este re-
caudo en manteca y aceite con unos chuchóte* huauchinan-
gos rajados, hasta que se refría mucho; entonces se le echa
una cucharada de vinagre y un pedacito de azúcar, se le
agrega un poco de apio picado para que se fría con el recau-

345

do; ya que está consumido el vinagre se le echa un chile
ancho remojado y molido con unas pimientas; se deja que
se fría y allí se voltean las lentejas y se dejan sazonar.

1.178. Jitomates rellenos. — Se les quita á los jitomates la
tapita de encima, se les saca lo de adentro y so pica cebolla,
caree de ternera, jamón y perejil; se revuelve todo y se frie
bien : con esto se rellenan los jitomates. Se unta una torte-
ra 6 sartén con manteca y se van poniendo los jitomates ya
rellenos, lo sobrante del picadillo con un poco de pan ralla-
do se les echa por encima, agregándoles un poquito de cal-
do y se oueoen á dos fuegos.

1.179. Jitomates rellenos. — Se quita el cabo de la parte
superior al jitomate para extraer las pepitas con una cucha-
ra de cafó, y se exprime el agua que contiene con una pre-
sión ligera con los dedos; se llena de una pasta compuesta
de perejil, pepinos, huevos cocidos duros y alcaparras, todo
picado muy finamente, anchoas en pedacitos, sal y aceite.
Lleno asi el jitomate, se envuelve en raspaduras de pan y
se pone en un hornillo.

1,11)8. Fresh white beans, homemade style. — Put them in boiling water with salt and a little butter; refresh them often with cold water; when they are cooked, drain them; put them in a saucepan with a good piece of butter, sauté them and add chopped parsley, salt and pepper, and a little vinegar or sour orange juice, and even better lemon juice.

1.169. White beans, Roman style. — Slice onions and fry them in oil, add the beans with chopped parsley, salt and pepper, and after everything has cooked for a while, put them on a plate, and pour over them a little boiled vinegar previously in a saucepan.

1.170. White beans. — *The white beans are cooked with a little tequesquite water; when they are cooked, they are washed thoroughly, as well as the pot in which they were cooked: in the same pot, clean water, lard and salt are added, it is put on the fire, a good amount of tomato without seeds is chopped and a little onion, a good amount of lard is put in a saucepan, the onion is fried, then the tomato and then the beans, they are left to boil until they thicken to serve them with oil, pickled chiles, etc.

1.171. Black beans. — The black beans are cooked without tequesquite, after being cooked they are emptied into a saucepan; a frying pan or saucepan is taken and they are fried with a good amount of lard and all kitchen condiments, cloves and cinnamon, chiles, olives, chorizos, longaniza and a little vinegar are ground for them.

1.172. Other brown beans. — After being cooked, they are washed and a little fried onion, ground red chile, some pieces of squab and other pieces of chicken breast are added to them; they must be loaded with lard, after which a little sherry wine is added to them.

1.173. Lentils, housewife’s style. — Cook the lentils in slightly salted water, drain them and put them in a saucepan with a good piece of lard, chopped parsley, salt and pepper; sauté them for a few minutes. Put them on the platter, garnishing them with fried bread crusts, and serve very hot.

1.174. Lentils, garden style. — Make pieces of onion and fine chopped herbs redden in butter: add flour; when the dough is made, moisten it with water, and even better with broth, add the lentils cooked in water and drained like the previous ones; add salt and pepper, sauté them the same way and serve.

1.175. Lentils with bacon, country style. — Put lentils and a good piece of ham in a pot full of water, cook them; when they are done, they are done like the previous ones and put on the platter on the ham in which they were cooked.

1.176. Lentils with parsley — They are cooked in water and salt, they are drained and then put in a saucepan with abundant lard, chopped parsley, salt and a little pepper, sauté them for a few minutes and serve with fried bread crusts, all very hot.

1.177. Lentils. — They are put to cook, and once they are cooked, a good amount of tomato, onion and garlic is chopped; this condiment is fried in lard and oil with some split chuchóte* huanznan-

345

gos, until it cools down a lot; then a spoonful of vinegar and a small piece of sugar are added to it, a little chopped celery is added to it so that it fries with the condiment; once the vinegar is consumed, a soaked and ground ancho chile with some peppercorns is added to it; it is left to fry and there the lentils are turned and left to season.

1.178. Stuffed tomatoes. — The top lid of the tomatoes is removed, the inside is taken out and onion, veal, ham and parsley are chopped; everything is mixed and fried well: with this the tomatoes are stuffed. A tortera or frying pan is greased with lard and the already stuffed tomatoes are placed in it, the leftover chopped mixture with a little breadcrumbs is poured over them, adding a little broth and they are cooked over two fires.

1.179. Stuffed tomatoes. — The top part of the tomato is removed to extract the seeds with a coffee spoon, and the water it contains is squeezed out with a light pressure with the fingers; it is filled with a paste composed of parsley, cucumbers, hard-boiled eggs and capers, all chopped very finely, anchovies in small pieces, salt and oil. Once the tomato is filled like this, it is wrapped in breadcrumbs and put in a small oven.

1.200. Zanahorias con jitomate. — Después de cocidas, se
parten en filetea y rehogan con manteca, perejil y cebolla
picada, un poco de sal y pimienta, y se echa una salsa de
jitomate por encima.

excerpts.translation: 1.200. Carrots with jitomate. — After being cooked, they are sliced into strips and sautéed with butter, parsley, and chopped onion, a little salt and pepper, and a sauce of jitomate is poured over them.

1,206. Calabazas cortadas. — Se escojen que no estén muy
recias y se cortan en rebanadas delgadas. Se ponen en el
fondo de una cazuela, se expolvorean con pimienta, sal y
jitomates picados, quitándoles antes el pellejo, para lo cual
se ponen sobre las brasas. Después se colocan otras lonjas
del mismo modo, se les baña de aceite crudo y se ponen á
dos fuegos. Es bueno echarles encima pan rallado, un poco
de yerbabuena y cebolla cortada muy moñuda.

352

1.209. Calabaza rehogada. — Se oorU en pedazos grandes,
se pone en una olla, con cebolla frita, ajos majados, pimien-
ta, tal y jitomate; te da vueltas hasta que está frito y se le
agrega un puñado de perejil y yerbabuena. Se les aftade
aceite cocido y pimienta.
1.210. Calabaza anisada. —Cortada en trozos se hace her-
vir un cuarto de hora con agua y sal y se escurre; se echa
en una cazuela un buen trozo de manteca y se fríe en ella,
sazonándola con especias y sal; hecho esto se coloca en un
plato, cubriendo los pedazos con queso rallado para que to-
men color, poniéndolos entre dos fuegos.

Una miga de pan empapada en leche, se exprime bien, se
le añaden dos yemas de huevo duro, dos onzas de queso ra-
llado, dos clavos, un batido de dos yemas; se pica y mezcla
todo muy bien; una vez lleno el hueco so enharinan las ce-
bollas, se bañan con yema de huevo y se f rien ; sírvanse in-
mediatamente bañándolas con salsa de jitomate 6 con zumo
de limón; pueden bañarse también con salsa de chile verde.
1 .220. A Iva-jones. — Se limpian , se ponen á cocer con agua
caliente y un poco de tequesquite, sin mojarlos de ningún
modo con agua fria; ya que estén cocidos se les echa agua
tibia y se escurren per tres veces hasta que el agua quede
muy limpia. Se les deja poca agua, se les echa una cucha-
rada de manteca con un poco de sal y se sazonan hasta que
queden espesos.

A breadcrumb soaked in milk is well squeezed, two hard egg yolks, two ounces of grated cheese, two cloves, a mixture of two yolks are added to it; everything is finely chopped and mixed very well; once the cavity is filled, the onions are floured, dipped in egg yolk and fried; serve immediately with tomato sauce or with lemon juice; they can also be served with green chili sauce.

1.220. A Iva-jones. — They are cleaned, put to cook with hot water and a little tequesquite, without wetting them in any way with cold water; once they are cooked, warm water is poured over them and they are drained three times until the water is very clean. They are left with little water, a spoonful of butter with a little salt is added to them and they are seasoned until they become thick.

excerpts.raw:
1.224. Garbanzos guisados. — Se pone á cocer garbanzo
gordo, y ya cocido se pela. Se muelen unos pocos muy re-
molidos con clavo y canela; se pica jitomate, cebolla y ajo,
se fríe bien y se le incorpora garbanzo á que se fría con el
jitomate; se le echa caldo de carne de puerco, costillas, re-
banadas de jamón, chorizos, los demás garbanzos enteros y
un pedazo de azúcar y vinagre. Se adorna con chiles en
vinagre.

excerpts.translation: 1.224. Stewed chickpeas. — Put thick chickpeas to cook, and once cooked, peel them. Grind a few very finely with cloves and cinnamon; chop tomatoes, onions, and garlic, fry well, and incorporate chickpeas to fry with the tomato; add pork broth, ribs, slices of ham, chorizos, the remaining whole chickpeas, and a piece of sugar and vinegar. Garnish with pickled chiles.
