1.269. Modo de hacer la conserva de jitomates, jqne aconse-
jamos adoptar, pnes es tan útil como ventajosa para atando
escasean los jitomates. — Varios son los modos de conservar
este fruto, pero el mejor de todos y el mas sencillo es con-
servarlos en conserva; e*sta se prepara del modo siguiente:
Se escojen los jitomates, se cortan á pedazos y se ponen al
fuego en un cazo que esté* bien estañado; cuando están bien
deshechos se pasa el zumo por un lienzo claro, se vuelve es-

te al fuego y se luce cocer hasta que te vuelva espeso como
£ punto de mermelada; conforme vaya adelantándose la ope-
ración se procurará que sea al fuego mas suave para que no
se requeme la conserva, y le quede buen color. Estando á
su punto se guarda en botes de loza, 6 bien puesta en plati-
llos se hace secar como pasta de dulce, y así se guarda en
paraje resguardado de la humedad en los mismos platillos;
antes se envuelve en papeles untados, con aceite.

1.270. Preparación de la maiUeca sin tal. — Se dividen en
trocí tos pequeños las mantecas del serdo, como igualmente
las de los riñónos, y se derriten á fuego manso. en vasija de
hierro 6 cobre, meneándola sin cesar hasta que se haya de-
rretido alguna parte, añádase, si se quiere, tomillo, laurel y
pimienta en rama, pero no sal, porque impediría la mezcla.
Actívese el fuego y cuando la grasa no despide humo es se-
ñal de que está cocida: entonces se cuela por tamiz bien tu*
pido, llenando loe tarros, que deben ser de barro, hasta el
borde. Se tapan con dos ó tres hojas de papel grueso en
lugar fresco.

1.271. Derretido y purificación de loe manteca*. — Se divi-
den en trocitos, separando las membranas y filamentos, se
echan en agua hirviendo, en donde permanecerán cociendo
un cuarto de hora, esparciéndolos bien. Saqúense después
para despachurrarlos en un plato con un tenedor. Esta es-
pecie de picadillo se vuelve á echar después en agua hirvien-
do para que cueza mansamente por espacio de una hora.
Cuélese después por una servilleta en una vasija, dejando
que se fije ó congele la grasa sobre la superficie del agua.
Se levanta oon cuidado y se limpia por debajo volviéndolo
á derretir de nuevo en baño de María, á fin de que suelte

In a casserole dish, half a pound of lard, one large tomato, and six cloves of chopped garlic, one head of onion are added and fried in the lard, after the fried seasoning the offal is added; two red chiles are soaked without toasting, they are ground and added, in addition a little bit of cloves and pepper; while boiling, four eggs are added, and when they are half cooked they are stirred; separately, pork meat, longaniza, chorizo, chorizos, and a very well golden chicken in portions are fried, and all this is added to it and to serve it, chiles in vinegar and olives are added.

Wrapped* of chüpocle and filled with beaten eggs.— The chilpocles are taken, they are burned, mulato chili and patilla are also taken, equal amounts of both, and of what is taken of chilpocle; these two kinds of chili are roasted and then put to soak; then the three kinds of chili are ground, some jitomates that are considered sufficient are roasted and ground: a cazuela is placed with a little fat on the fire, and once this is burned, the chili is added so that it becomes well fried, then the jitomate is incorporated and the broth of the pork meat is added so that it becomes well thickened and seasoned with salt to taste. 1.436. Tinga of nuco chile. — The chiles are wilted raw the day before and put in salt water; the next day that water is removed, they are shredded, put to fry in lard and a little oil with tomato, onion and garlic, all finely chopped; once it is well fried, water, salt and some tender sliced zucchini are added. Once everything is cooked, it is removed from the heat, garnished with fried loin meat, longaniza, chorizos, ribs and chorison, all fried; and on top sliced onion, avocado, lettuce, radish, oil and aged cheese.

1.437. Bacalao à la Toluca with ancho chile. — The ancho chile is soaked from the night before in a good quantity, in proportion to the cod, and is wilted; the next day it is ground with garlic, pepper and clove: this is fried in oil and the rest in lard; when both things are ready they are incorporated with the mentioned broth and the raw cod is added. It is left to cook and is thickened with soaked ground bread. It is served by pouring on top oil, chopped parsley, olives and tornachiles made into pieces.

1.438. Bacalao codeflo. — The cod is soaked from one day to the next and put to cook in a well-covered pot. Onion, tomato and garlic are chopped; some green chiles are roasted and made into strips. This ingredient must be in double the quantity of the cod that is being cooked or at least must be put in the following proportion:

57

For one pound of cod, eight chiles and twelve tomatoes are taken, which are not to be chopped much, but rather the pieces should remain thick.

1.668. “Empernada” — To one pound of flour, two egg yolks are added and kneaded very strongly so that the dough remains smooth, and to knead it, a little warm water with salt is added; when well kneaded, it is rolled out with a rolling pin and a little of the filling is placed on top of the dough; about one spoonful in each empanada; then the dough is folded and cut with the wheel, giving it the usual shape. A good amount of butter is heated and, when very hot, the empanadas are fried until golden, and the following filling is added:

Large pieces of veal and pork meat are chopped and cooked with salt. After being well cooked, it is finely chopped so that it becomes very finely minced and fried with a little tomato, onion, and garlic, which must be well fried before adding the meat. When halfway fried, a little vinegar is added and it is left to dry until the meat becomes very golden.

1.784. Jicama cake. — The slices are made very thin, they are mixed with chopped carrots, everything is put in syrup of medium point and it is being preserved with its odors to the wind; all this is ground, a layer of mamón is put and another of potato, pill and sesame on top of each layer.

1.785. Coconut cake. — When [illegible] the brown skin is removed from it, it is grated or ground; it is put in syrup of medium point and it is preserved; raisins, almonds and odors are put, a layer of this and another of mamón, pill and sesame on top,

1.786. Tomato cake. — The ripe tomatoes and roasted in the oven on a board; [illegible] then in a napkin they are squeezed [illegible] that no juice remains of them; to each quart of this juice half a pound of white sugar with a strip of cinnamon, six cloves, a piece of nutmeg and all ground is put to boil until it becomes syrup; to it

171

is put a small cup of white wine and a layer of mamón is put and another of the mixture, on top pill and cinnamon.

1.787. Palace cake. — Fifty eggs are taken and put to cook until they harden, the yolks must be sifted with a bristle sieve; a quarter of sugar is clarified; a pound of ground almonds is put until the sugar takes point, all this is taken out, it is put in the syrup already at point, the layers of mamón and what is said are put.

1.788. Cottage cheese cake. — The cottage cheese is ground and put in syrup with egg yolks and odor; it is cooked and put on mamón soaked with syrup, and on top all its requirements.

1.789. Milk cake. — In the milk are put enough egg yolks, sugar, cinnamon, orange blossom water and odor, all competent, [illegible] taste; layers of mamón are put and they are moistened, so that they remain very well soaked, and putting on all the layers all their requirements and their cinnamon powder; first the pot is greased with butter to put said layers; so that everything is put it is put to cook between two fires or in oven, with cinnamon on top.

1.790. Egg cake. — A pound of clarified sugar is thickened to medium point; since this is so it is put to cool, to it are put six egg yolks, the skin is removed from them and they are mixed very well, so that it remains of good color; it is put on the fire until it is thick like atole; it is set aside and since it is cold mamón is sliced and soaked in syrup of medium point and enough wine; a layer of egg is put and another of mamón and so it continues being the last of egg, putting on top cinnamon, raisins, almonds, pine nuts and citron.

643. Duck stuffed. — The ducks are skinned and gutted, and after being well washed and the rump removed, they are put in a pot with water and straw, and once they have given a few boils they are removed from the heat, they are given one or two washings with hot water, after which they are cut into quarters, butter is put in a saucepan and the ducks are put in there with some slices of ham and plenty of chopped onion and garlic and everything is left to fry well. After this water and a little chopped parsley, thyme and oregano are added, and clove, cinnamon and pepper are ground with some slices of fried bread. The dish is garnished with chiles, asparagus and olives.

744. Another duck. — The same is done as in the previous one until where it says that the butter is put in a saucepan.

When this is hot the ducks are put in, two or three tomatoes and two bunches of onion and a little chopped parsley, and this is put in with the meat: once everything is fried flour is added and it is left to fry a little more; then water is added, clove, cinnamon and pepper are ground, it is put in the stew and it is garnished as in the previous one. It has to remain like a thin broth.

746. Another duck. — The same is done as in the previous ones. A small saucepan is greased with butter, garlic, parsley and onion are chopped, slices of ham, and everything is fried together with the duck. Some thin turnips are chopped and they are fried with butter; together with clove, cinnamon and pepper and another layer is put in where everything is; water is added to it so that it simmers; other turnips are sliced and they are put in; slices of bread are fried, they are ground and they are added to it; the stew has to remain thick and before removing it from the heat they are put with sherry. It is garnished as the previous ones.

746. Stuffed duck. — After being cooked with straw and all the rumps removed, they are cleaned and dried with a cloth, they are boned and rolled in flour, they are fried in butter, they are taken out and they are put in layers inside a pot. 757. Another of agachona*. — They are skinned and opened and the entrails, gizzards and liver* are joined. Butter is put in a casserole and the agachonas with pieces of ham are put there, quite finely chopped onion, a little garlic also chopped. The entrails, gizzards and liver, after being washed and ground, are fried and put in the casserole with a little carlon wine, clear, cinnamon, pepper and a little thyme.
